subject: ParcelPilot deployment fit — hosted feasibility questions and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: ParcelPilot deployment fit — hosted feasibility questions and next steps

Hi Emma / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great to see your vector search + routing use case in action. Quick recap from our side and a few items we need to lock down to scope a short hosted pilot: 

- Primary ask: confirm whether you want to start with Redwood Hosted (fastest to launch) or evaluate Dedicated/Private for predictable throughput and network isolation.
- Pilot goals: 1) validate response quality on your 3 canonical prompts, 2) measure 95th percentile latency under expected concurrency, 3) validate embedding recall for search.
- Key inputs we need from you: expected steady-state QPS per endpoint, peak burst QPS, typical request token length, and whether you need VPC/private endpoints or are comfortable with hosted endpoints.

I've attached a short evaluation checklist to guide the pilot (parcelpilot_eval_checklist.pdf) and a quick snapshot of our default rate-limit tiers. Short answers to the bullets above will let us size the hosted configuration and propose a pilot rate-limit increase if needed.

Proposed immediate next step: 30-minute technical call with Samir + your infra person to walk through endpoints and sample payloads. Here’s a Calendly link for availability: https://calendly.com/redwood/parcelpilot-tech-30m

If you prefer not to share traffic estimates yet, we can run a small synthetic spike test on the hosted environment (we'll need your test API key and representative payloads).

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: ParcelPilot deployment fit — hosted feasibility questions and next steps

Thanks Ben — useful checklist. A few clarification items from our side before we book the tech call: 

1) Rate limits: what are the default and burst limits for the hosted API? We expect to start around 30 QPS for chat/generation (peak 120 QPS during campaigns) and ~250 embedding requests/minute when we batch.
2) Isolation / data residency: can hosted provide per-tenant data isolation and optional private endpoints (VPC peering)? We have some regulated partners asking about network separation.
3) Logging & compliance: data retention windows, access to audit logs, and options for customer-managed keys (KMS).
4) Quickstart: can you send an example curl for your streaming /v1/chat and the embeddings endpoint so our infra team can validate request/response shape?

If hosted can't meet the isolation/rate needs comfortably, we want to understand the delta/cost to move to Dedicated or Private.

Thanks — Emma

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Holt <emma.holt@parcelpilot.com>, Samir Desai <samir@parcelpilot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ParcelPilot deployment fit — hosted feasibility questions and next steps

Hi Emma — great questions. Short answers below, with suggested next steps. I also attached a snapshot of our rate-limit tiers (rate_limits_snapshot.png).

1) Rate limits (Hosted):
- Default: text generation/chat endpoints = 60 requests/min per API key (sustained).
- Embeddings endpoint = 120 requests/min per API key (sustained).
- Burst handling: we allow short bursts up to ~3x sustained for very short windows; for predictable higher bursts we issue a trial increase for pilots (subject to monitoring).
- Note: rate limits can be raised for pilots to match your 120 QPS peak; for long-term 24/7 high QPS we recommend Dedicated capacity.

2) Isolation / private networking:
- Hosted: logical tenant isolation is standard; Hosted does not provide customer-managed hardware or private on-prem networks.
- Hosted + VPC: for customers requiring network separation we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) with a private control plane and optional VPC peering or direct connect.
- Dedicated: provides isolated GPU pools and higher committed throughput but still runs in Redwood-managed infra; we can map out IP allow-lists and tighter tenancy controls.

3) Logging & compliance:
- Default data retention: 30 days for request/response logs in the hosted offering; audit logs available for 90 days with add-on retention.
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we can share a SOC 2 report under NDA.
- KMS: customer-managed keys available on Private; Hosted supports envelope encryption and restricted access but not customer KMS by default.

4) Quickstart curl samples (minimal):
- Chat (streaming):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-4x-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the order issues"}],"stream":true}'

- Embeddings:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-text-embed-1","input":["order #1234 issue text"]}'

Suggested next steps:
- Please confirm target steady/peak QPS and a representative sample payload (max 512 tokens) so we can pre-configure a pilot key and request a temporary rate-limit increase.
- Schedule the technical 30-min: https://calendly.com/redwood/parcelpilot-tech-30m

If you'd like, we can provision a short Dedicated trial (30 days) for predictable latency during your campaign window — I can loop in Solutions (Lauren) for costs/commit sizing.

Best,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: ParcelPilot — internal next-step recommendation

Ben / Lauren — quick internal note. ParcelPilot looks like a good fit for a hosted pilot with a temporary rate-limit bump to validate the campaign peak. Recommended approach:

- Offer a 30-day hosted pilot with rate limits raised to ~200 requests/min for chat and 400/min for embeddings for the pilot period; measure 95p latency and decide within 30 days.
- If they need strict network isolation or sustained >200 QPS, propose Dedicated sizing options and include a cost delta.
- Prepare a short SOW addendum for the pilot (include success criteria from Ben's checklist).

I'll draft a pilot SOW and a templated pilot discount (mid-market). Ben — can you confirm their exact peak/steady numbers after the tech call and we can finalize the pilot offer?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Ben — thanks for the detail, that helps a lot. We want to start with a hosted pilot and will provide:

- Steady QPS targets: 30 QPS generation, peak 120 QPS (campaign spikes).
- Embedding pattern: batch up to 500 items/min during sync windows.
- No regulatory requirement for immediate VPC; SOC2 report and 90-day audit logs would be sufficient for our Security team for now.

I booked the tech slot on your Calendly for Friday at 10:00am PT. We'll bring Samir (CTO) and our infra lead. Looking forward to the pilot SOW and the temporary rate-limit increase.

Best,
Emma
